newsHook: Winning Best Business Leader at the Modern Barber Awards, for running a barbering group rather than a single chair, is exactly the kind of story our readers do not hear often enough.
questions: Best Business Leader is an award for running the business, not for cutting hair. Which of those is the harder job?
Murdock has several shops. What breaks first when a barbershop becomes a group?
How do you keep the standard identical across sites when the product is a person's hands?
Barbering has very high staff turnover. What actually makes a barber stay?
What do you know about the economics of a chair now that you wish you had known at the first shop?
Grooming retail and services pull in different directions. How do you decide where the money goes?
Where does Murdock London go from here?

newsHook: Winning Best Social Barber at the Modern Barber Awards, in a trade where social media has become the shop window, is a story our readers would genuinely learn from.
questions: You won an award for social media in a trade built on walk-ins. How much of your business now starts on a phone?
Most barbers post constantly and get nothing back. What are they doing wrong?
What kind of post actually fills a chair, as opposed to getting likes?
Being visible online invites opinions. What has that cost you?
How much time does it really take, and who does it in your shop?
Platforms change the rules every year. How do you build on ground that keeps moving?
Where does Novo Cabelo go from here?

newsHook: Winning Best Photographic Image at the Modern Barber Awards, on top of building a global mentoring programme for barbers, is exactly the kind of story our readers want more of.
questions: You won for a photograph. How much of a modern barber's reputation is made by the picture rather than the cut?
Mentored by Menspire puts you in the teaching business as well as the barbering one. What made you build it?
What do barbers ask you for most often, and what do they actually need?
You work internationally. What does British barbering do better than anywhere else, and what does it do worse?
What is the most common mistake a talented barber makes when they open their own shop?
How do you protect your own time when your name is the brand?
Where does MENSPIRE go from here?
